atoms.text: This guide configures MirrorLane, a replication service that copies new objects from a primary bucket to a disaster recovery bucket in a second region. The destination bucket, dr-replica-usw, and the replication role, MirrorLaneReplicationRole, both belong to account 111111111111. Access is granted only through the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy on dr-replica-usw is left unchanged. Attach a policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging, and s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw and arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw/*. Confirm that versioning is enabled on the destination bucket, because MirrorLane rejects replication rules whose target is unversioned. In IAM, verify that the role's trust policy lists the MirrorLane service principal so the service can assume the role. Create the replication rule with the prefix filter backups/ and set the destination storage class to STANDARD_IA. Upload a test object under backups/ and check that it appears in dr-replica-usw within a few minutes with its original tags. If the object does not arrive, review the role's attached policy for a missing action or resource ARN.

This guide configures MirrorLane, a replication service that copies new objects from a primary bucket to a disaster recovery bucket in a second region. The destination bucket, dr-replica-usw, belongs to account 222222222222, while the replication role, MirrorLaneReplicationRole, belongs to account 111111111111. The bucket owner grants access by adding a statement to the bucket policy of dr-replica-usw that names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/MirrorLaneReplicationRole as the principal. The statement allows s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectTagging, and s3:GetBucketVersioning on arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw and arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw/*, and the role's own identity-based policy in account 111111111111 must list the same actions. Confirm that versioning is enabled on the destination bucket, because MirrorLane rejects replication rules whose target is unversioned. In IAM, verify that the role's trust policy lists the MirrorLane service principal so the service can assume the role. Create the replication rule with the prefix filter backups/ and set the destination storage class to STANDARD_IA. Upload a test object under backups/ and check that it appears in dr-replica-usw within a few minutes with its original tags. If the object does not arrive, review the bucket policy in account 222222222222 for a missing action, resource ARN, or incorrect principal.

This guide sets up DumpKeeper, an agent that uploads nightly database dumps from a database host to a backup bucket. The bucket, db-backups-prod, and the upload role, DumpKeeperUploadRole, are both in account 111111111111. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, and no change is made to the bucket policy of db-backups-prod. Add a policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::db-backups-prod and arn:aws:s3:::db-backups-prod/nightly/*. Dumps larger than 100 MB are sent as multipart uploads, so the multipart actions must be present or large uploads will fail partway. Configure the agent with the role name and set its target prefix to nightly/ so each dump is written as nightly/YYYY-MM-DD/dump.sql.gz. Run the agent in dry-run mode first to confirm that it can assume the role and start a multipart upload. Then run a manual dump and confirm the object is listed under the expected key. If the agent returns AccessDenied, check the role's policy for the correct bucket name and prefix.

The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement that names arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/DumpKeeperUploadRole as the principal. The statement allows s3:PutObject, s3:AbortMultipartUpload, and s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads on arn:aws:s3:::db-backups-prod and arn:aws:s3:::db-backups-prod/nightly/*, and the role's identity-based policy in account 111111111111 must allow the same actions. Dumps larger than 100 MB are sent as multipart uploads, so the multipart actions must be present or large uploads will fail partway. Configure the agent with the role ARN and set its target prefix to nightly/ so each dump is written as nightly/YYYY-MM-DD/dump.sql.gz. Run the agent in dry-run mode first to confirm that it can assume the role and start a multipart upload. Then run a manual dump and confirm the object is listed under the expected key. If the agent returns AccessDenied, check the bucket policy for the correct role ARN, bucket name, and prefix.

This guide prepares FailoverRestore, a job that reads replicated objects from a disaster recovery bucket and loads them into a standby environment. The bucket, dr-replica-usw, and the job's role, FailoverRestoreRole, are in the same account, 111111111111. Access is granted solely through the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of dr-replica-usw stays as it is. Attach a policy that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw, plus s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw/*. The version actions are required because the job restores a specific version ID recorded in its restore manifest. The job performs no writes to the bucket, so omit any s3:PutObject or s3:DeleteObject permissions. Set the job's source to dr-replica-usw and its restore point to a manifest key such as manifests/restore-2025-03-01.json. Start a test restore of a small prefix and compare the object count and checksums with the manifest. If a key is skipped, confirm that the role's policy covers the full resource path of that key.

This guide prepares FailoverRestore, a job that reads replicated objects from a disaster recovery bucket and loads them into a standby environment. The bucket, dr-replica-usw, is owned by account 222222222222, and the job's role, FailoverRestoreRole, belongs to account 111111111111. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement with arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/FailoverRestoreRole as the principal. The statement allows s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw, plus s3:GetObject, s3:GetObjectVersion, and s3:GetObjectTagging on arn:aws:s3:::dr-replica-usw/*, and the role's own identity-based policy must list the same actions. The version actions are required because the job restores a specific version ID recorded in its restore manifest. The job performs no writes to the bucket, so omit any s3:PutObject or s3:DeleteObject permissions. Set the job's source to dr-replica-usw and its restore point to a manifest key such as manifests/restore-2025-03-01.json. Start a test restore of a small prefix and compare the object count and checksums with the manifest. If a key is skipped, confirm that the bucket policy covers the full resource path of that key.

This guide configures LockStep, a service that writes immutable backup copies to a bucket with Object Lock enabled. The bucket, vault-immutable-01, and the service role, LockStepWriterRole, are both in account 111111111111. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of vault-immutable-01 is not modified. Add a policy to the role that allows s3:PutObject, s3:PutObjectRetention, and s3:GetBucketObjectLockConfiguration on arn:aws:s3:::vault-immutable-01 and arn:aws:s3:::vault-immutable-01/*. Object Lock must have been enabled when the bucket was created, because it cannot be turned on for an existing bucket without a support request. Set the default retention in the LockStep job to compliance mode for 35 days. Each backup object is uploaded with a retain-until date computed from the job's start time. Upload a test object and use a head request to confirm the retention mode and date are present. If uploads fail with a retention error, verify that s3:PutObjectRetention appears in the role's policy.

This guide covers HashCheck, a verification job that reads backup objects and compares their checksums against a recorded catalog. The backup bucket, backup-store-east, and the job's role, HashCheckReaderRole, are both in account 111111111111. Access is granted only through the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of backup-store-east is unchanged. Attach a policy that allows s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::backup-store-east and s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectAttributes on arn:aws:s3:::backup-store-east/archives/*. The job requests object attributes to retrieve stored SHA-256 checksums without downloading each full object. HashCheck is read-only and writes its results to a local log file, so no write actions are needed on the bucket. Configure the job with a schedule of weekly and a sampling rate of 10 percent of keys under archives/. Run it once manually and confirm that the log reports the number of objects checked and any mismatches. If listing succeeds but attribute requests fail, check that the role's policy includes the object-level resource path.

This guide sets up TrimPolicy, a retention job that deletes expired backup versions from a bucket after a defined period. The bucket, snapshots-archive, and the job's role, TrimPolicyRole, are both in account 111111111111. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of snapshots-archive is not edited. Add a policy that allows s3:ListBucket and s3:ListBucketVersions on arn:aws:s3:::snapshots-archive, and s3:DeleteObject and s3:DeleteObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::snapshots-archive/snapshots/*. Restricting the delete actions to the snapshots/ prefix prevents the job from removing objects stored elsewhere in the bucket. Configure TrimPolicy with a retention window of 90 days, based on each object's last-modified time. The job lists versions under snapshots/, selects those older than the window, and deletes them in batches of 500 keys. Run the job with the report-only flag first to review the candidate list before enabling deletion. If a batch returns partial errors, check that the role's policy covers both the delete and version-listing actions.

This guide configures SnapExport, a tool that copies application file snapshots to a backup bucket using a dedicated IAM user rather than a role. The bucket, app-snapshots-eu, and the IAM user, snapexport-user, are both in account 111111111111. Access is granted only through the user's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of app-snapshots-eu is left untouched. Attach a policy to the user that allows s3:PutObject and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::app-snapshots-eu, limiting object writes to arn:aws:s3:::app-snapshots-eu/exports/billing/*. Generate an access key for the user, store it in the SnapExport credentials file with restrictive file permissions, and rotate it every 90 days. Set the tool's destination prefix to exports/billing/ and enable server-side checksum verification on upload. Each run writes a compressed archive named snapshot-YYYYMMDD.tar.zst and does not read or overwrite earlier archives. Run the tool once and confirm that the archive appears under the prefix with a matching checksum. If an upload is denied, confirm that the key path begins with exports/billing/.

Generate an access key for the user, store it in the SnapExport credentials file with restrictive file permissions, and rotate it every 90 days. Each run writes a compressed archive named snapshot-YYYYMMDD.tar.zst and does not read or overwrite earlier archives. If an upload is denied, confirm that the key path begins with exports/billing/ and that the bucket policy names the correct user.

This guide prepares CatalogSync, a service that maintains a backup catalog by reading the previous catalog file and writing an updated one after each backup run. The bucket, backup-catalog-main, and the service role, CatalogSyncRole, are in the same account, 111111111111. Access is granted only by the role's identity-based policy, and the bucket policy of backup-catalog-main is not changed. Attach a policy that allows s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::backup-catalog-main/catalog/*, and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::backup-catalog-main with a prefix condition of catalog/. After each run, the service reads catalog/current.json, merges the new entries, and writes the result as catalog/current.json and a dated copy under catalog/history/. Enable versioning on the bucket so that an interrupted write can be rolled back to the earlier catalog. Configure the service with the bucket name and the role name, and set the write timeout to 60 seconds. Trigger a test run and confirm that both the current and dated files are updated. If the read step fails on a first run, check that catalog/current.json exists or that the service is set to initialize it.

This guide prepares CatalogSync, a service that maintains a backup catalog by reading the previous catalog file and writing an updated one after each backup run. The bucket, backup-catalog-main, is owned by account 222222222222, and the service role, CatalogSyncRole, belongs to account 111111111111. The bucket owner grants access by adding a bucket policy statement that names the account ID 111111111111 as the principal, so that identities in that account can be authorized by their own policies. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::backup-catalog-main/catalog/*, and s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::backup-catalog-main with a prefix condition of catalog/, while CatalogSyncRole's identity-based policy allows the same actions. After each run, the service reads catalog/current.json, merges the new entries, and writes the result as catalog/current.json and a dated copy under catalog/history/. Enable versioning on the bucket so that an interrupted write can be rolled back to the earlier catalog. Configure the service with the bucket name and the role ARN, and set the write timeout to 60 seconds. Trigger a test run and confirm that both the current and dated files are updated. If the read step fails on a first run, check that catalog/current.json exists or that the service is set to initialize it.
